= CI/CD Workflow Catalog

*Purpose:* Central registry of all available CI/CD workflows for the hyperpolymath and metadatastician estates.

*Maintained by:* Estate-wide standards *Source of Truth:* This file + `rsr-template-repo/.github/workflows/` + `standards/.github/workflows/`

'''''

== How to Use This Catalog

=== For New Repos

When creating a new repo, select workflows from this catalog based on your needs:

* *All repos* should have: governance.yml, codeql.yml, scorecard.yml, hypatia-scan.yml
* *Rust repos* should also have: rust-ci.yml, cflite_pr.yml, cflite_batch.yml
* *Elixir repos* should also have: elixir-ci.yml
* *Julia repos* should also have: julia-ci.yml
* *Guix-managed repos* should also have: guix-policy.yml

=== For Existing Repos

Use this catalog to:

[arabic]
. Identify missing workflows your repo should have
. Find the correct workflow name and source
. Copy workflows from the canonical sources

=== Workflow Sources

* *Template workflows:* `hyper-repos/_RSR _SET/rsr-template-repo/.github/workflows/`
* *Reusable workflows:* `hyper-repos/standards/.github/workflows/` (call these, don't copy)
* *Specialized workflows:* Listed below with their canonical repo

'''''

[cols=",,,",options="header",]
|===
|Workflow |Description |Source |Reusable?
|`elixir-ci.yml` |Elixir build and test |rsr-template-repo |No
|`elixir-ci-reusable.yml` |Reusable Elixir CI |standards |Yes
|`echidna-verify.yml` |ECHIDNA trust-pipeline proof verification (Agda/Idris2). NOT the smart-contract fuzzer. Corpora are evicted to their own repos; surviving jobs (`agda-lol`, `idris2-avow`) open with a presence Guard and pass green-but-honest ("Nothing to type-check") until a corpus returns (#748/#828). The `idris2-a2ml` job is EVICTED as of 2026-09-17: the a2ml project is officially retired (owner ruling), so dormancy was moot — no ruleset pinned its check context (verified live: org ruleset Optimus-Branch #23359343). |standards |Yes
|===

*Elixir note — `mix local.rebar` fails against builds.hex.pm on older OTP builds.* Erlang/OTP rejects that host's current Let's Encrypt chain (`key_usage_mismatch` on the `YR1` intermediate), so `erlef/setup-beam` dies in the setup step within seconds:

....
** (Mix) httpc request failed with: {:failed_connect, [{:to_address, {~c"builds.hex.pm", 443}},
  {:inet, [:inet], {:tls_alert, {:unsupported_certificate, ... {key_usage_mismatch, ...}}}}}]}
Could not install Rebar because Mix could not download metadata at
https://builds.hex.pm/installs/rebar3-1.x.csv.
....

It is *version-specific and fixed upstream*: on the same day, against the same host and the same action pin, OTP 27.3.4.17 (erts-15.2.7.13) succeeds where 27.2.1 (erts-15.2.1) fails — measured 2026-09-19 (chimichanga passing, bofig failing). *Bump `otp-version` to a current patch release*; the pinned OTP build is the cause, not the environment.

Passing `rebar3-version` does *not* avoid this: setup-beam runs `mix local.rebar` _before_ it considers that input, gated only by `install-rebar` (default true) — so a rebar3 pin cannot bypass the cert error, and bofig spent three months red because it assumed otherwise. To skip the call itself, set `install-rebar: false` (and `install-hex: false` if Hex is not needed from hex.pm). If you do set `rebar3-version`, pass `github-token` too — the version lookup otherwise hits api.github.com unauthenticated.

== Git Hooks Catalog

In addition to GitHub Actions workflows, the estate uses git hooks for local validation.

=== Available Hooks

All hooks are available in `hyper-repos/standards/.githooks/` and can be installed via:

[source,bash]
----
# In any repo:
git config core.hooksPath .githooks
# Or copy from standards:
cp -r /home/hyperpolymath/developer/hyper-repos/standards/.githooks .
chmod +x .githooks/*
git config core.hooksPath .githooks
----

[cols=",,,",options="header",]
|===
|Hook |Trigger |Description |Blocking?
|`pre-commit` |Before commit |Language policy, SPDX headers, K9 validation, workflow validation, canonical names, bot directives (the A2ML manifests gate was removed 2026-09-15, owner ruling R-H3: A2ML is retired — DEED is the grammar; a grammar-faithful .deed validator returns per R-H2) |Yes
|`pre-push` |Before push |Local Dogfood Gate (full validation: K9, SPDX, workflows, secrets scan — A2ML gate removed per R-H3) |Yes
|`commit-msg` |Before commit message saved |Conventional commits format, issue references, subject length, body presence |Yes
|`post-merge` |After merge/pull |Auto-deployment, submodule init, environment reminders (virtualenv, node_modules, Cargo.lock) |No
|`post-checkout` |After branch checkout |Environment setup reminders, dependency notices, branch protection warnings |No
|`pre-rebase` |Before rebase |Prevent rebase onto main/master, block protected branch rebasing, check uncommitted changes |Yes
|===

=== Hook Installation

[arabic]
. *Copy hooks to your repo:*
+
[source,bash]
----
mkdir -p .githooks
cp /home/hyperpolymath/developer/hyper-repos/standards/.githooks/* .githooks/
chmod +x .githooks/*
----
. *Enable hooks:*
+
[source,bash]
----
git config core.hooksPath .githooks
----
. *Verify:*
+
[source,bash]
----
git config core.hooksPath  # Should output: .githooks
----

=== Hook Propagation

The estate uses an automated system to keep hooks synchronized:

* *Trigger:* Push to `.githooks/` in standards repo
* *Workflow:* `propagate-hooks.yml`
* *Target:* All repos in hyperpolymath and metadatastician orgs
* *Method:* Uses `--force-with-lease` for safe updates

=== Bypassing Hooks

All hooks can be bypassed when necessary:

[source,bash]
----
git commit --no-verify
git push --no-verify
git rebase --no-verify
----

Use sparingly - only when certain it's a false positive.

[[pattern-relevance-gated-heavy-work-gate--skip]]
== Pattern: Relevance-Gated Heavy Work (gate + skip)

Heavy jobs — full test suites, proof checkers, expensive builds — do not need to run on every pull request, but their required checks must _post_ on every pull request or branch protection deadlocks. This pattern resolves both.

*The trap it prevents.* A required check from a path-filtered workflow never posts on a PR that matches no path (`on.pull_request.paths`), so the required context can never be satisfied and the PR is blocked with nothing red to look at. This has been sprung in the estate at least twice (MetaManifold-WebUI #39, and the occupancy checks on #116's squash).

*The pattern.* Keep the workflow trigger unfiltered, add a cheap gate job that always runs and decides relevance from the changed paths, and give the heavy jobs `needs: [gate]` + `if: needs.<gate>.outputs.relevant == 'true'`. When the gate says not relevant, GitHub posts `skipped` for the heavy jobs, and *a skipped check satisfies a required check*. The gate itself must never be skipped — it is the check that vouches for the others' absence — so require it too.

*Reference implementations* (copy the hardening, not just the shape):

* `hyperpolymath/MetaManifold-WebUI` `.github/workflows/occupancy.yml` — the `Occupancy relevance` gate (PR #125) and its two reading jobs.
* `hyperpolymath/MetaManifold-WebUI` `.github/workflows/ci.yml` — the `Code relevance` gate (PR #156) in front of `Julia tests` (~19 min) and `Agda proofs`.

*Hardening both reviews demanded:*

* `git diff --no-renames --name-only -z`, read NUL-delimited (`while IFS= read -r -d '' file`) — a file renamed out of a listed path is reported as a deletion under its original name, and a pathname Git would quote arrives raw.
* The diff base reaches the script through `env:`, never `${{ }}` interpolation inside `run:` (zizmor's template-injection rule).
* Quote *every* pattern in the array: an unquoted `src/*` expands against the checkout at assignment time; the glob must fire at `case` time, against the diff.
* The path list is the _positive_ form (anything not listed is not relevant), so a new directory joins the suite by being added, not forgotten — and paths the tests themselves read (workflow files, shape inputs, doc-shaped proof trees) must be listed even though they look irrelevant.
* The gate job's name is a stable identifier with no matrix, like every other check a ruleset matches by display name.

*When not to use it.* If the heavy work is the only check and cheap enough, or if the suite cannot distinguish relevant from irrelevant paths safely, run everything on everything — the deadlock only bites the combination _path-filtered trigger_ + _required check_.

== How to Add a Workflow to a Repo

=== For Reusable Workflows

These should *call* the reusable workflow instead of copying:

Note: `governance-reusable.yml`, `hypatia-scan-reusable.yml` and `secret-scanner-reusable.yml` are deprecated for new repositories. The rsr-template-repo template runs those three checks as inline jobs; new repositories should use the inline form. Existing callers pinned by SHA keep working.

[source,yaml]
----
jobs:
  governance:
    # Grant exactly what the callee declares (governance-reusable asks for
    # actions: read + contents: read). A called workflow can never exceed
    # its caller's grant, and a job-level block REPLACES the workflow-level
    # one — under-granting here rejects the run at startup.
    permissions:
      actions: read
      contents: read
    uses: metadatastician/standards/.github/workflows/governance-reusable.yml@<full-40-char-commit-sha>
    # Add a `secrets:` block ONLY when the callee declares named secrets
    # under `workflow_call.secrets`, passing each by name. Never use
    # `secrets: inherit` — it forwards every repo/org secret the caller
    # can see (standards#1108 §6b). Most reusables (e.g. the secret
    # scanner) declare none and need no `secrets:` line at all.
----

=== For Non-Reusable Workflows

Copy the workflow file from the source repo:

[source,bash]
----
cp /home/hyperpolymath/developer/hyper-repos/_RSR _SET/rsr-template-repo/.github/workflows/WORKFLOW.yml \
   /path/to/your/repo/.github/workflows/WORKFLOW.yml
----
